overview: Sigma's Catch is a fall and void catcher with two modes. When the client-side fallDistance exceeds the configured threshold, default 5, and the void-only option is satisfied, the Hypixel mode, the default, sends a C04PacketPlayerPosition lifting the player 12 blocks, while the Motion mode writes motionY = 0 into the EventMove instead of sending anything. A saveMe flag latched through a 150ms Timer paces the catches, and every catch resets the local fallDistance to zero.

sections.p: The module listens to EventMove only. Each event first clears saveMe when 150ms have passed or the player collides vertically, then evaluates the catch condition: fallDistance above the DIST setting, the Fly module disabled, and, when the VOID option is on, no block under the player, where isBlockUnder steps the bounding box down in 2-block increments and collides it against the world. On a catch it latches saveMe, resets the timer, zeroes mc.thePlayer.fallDistance and runs the selected mode. The MODE and DIST settings use Sigma's Setting constructor, (name, value, desc, inc, min, max), so DIST 5 with inc 1, min 4 and max 10 means the fall threshold sits between 4 and 10 blocks.

The Hypixel mode sends new C03PacketPlayer.C04PacketPlayerPosition(posX, posY + 12, posZ, false), an onGround-false position packet that lifts the player 12 blocks in one move. Because the catch resets the local fallDistance, the next C04 fires only after another 5 blocks of fall accumulate, roughly every 9 ticks, so the void stream is a periodic +12 lift on top of the vanilla C03s. The Motion mode writes em.setY(mc.thePlayer.motionY = 0), which caps the descent in the move event with no packet of its own. Vanilla's moved-too-quickly gate squares min(delta, motion) per axis, and with server-side motion small at catch time the +12 lift stays under the 100 threshold, so a stock server accepts the stream.

The client-side fallDistance = 0 reset is purely local; the server tracks its own fall height and applies fall damage from it on landing. The module's real wire fingerprint is the periodic C04 ascension, which movement envelopes score per move rather than per claimed flag. In the void the lift is what keeps the player alive, and it is also what an anticheat sees first: a repeated instant 12-block ascent is the strongest possible vertical anomaly in the stream, far beyond any jump envelope.

files.label: Catch.java (fall catcher)
files.explanation: The whole module. The EventMove handler clears the saveMe latch after 150ms or on vertical collision, then checks the fall distance against DIST, the Fly module state and the VOID block-under scan. On a catch it resets fallDistance and runs the selected mode: Hypixel sends the C04 position packet with y plus 12 and onGround false, Motion zeroes motionY through the move event. isBlockUnder steps the bounding box down in 2-block increments from the current y, which is what decides void falls: below y 0 it returns false immediately, so the catch fires over open void.

files.label: EventMove.java (motion carrier)
files.explanation: EventMove carries the x, y and z components of the tick's move, fired by the movement hook with the three deltas. The Motion mode uses em.setY to write the y component the movement system applies for the tick, paired with the direct mc.thePlayer.motionY = 0 write, which caps the descent with no packet of its own. The x and z components stay untouched, so the mode only removes vertical momentum; the file also shows why the Hypixel mode bypasses the event entirely: it builds its own C04 rather than editing the move.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (movement physics envelope)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly allows vertical distance from the previous move's momentum and accepts only a small set of named envelopes, grounded zero-y moves, jumps and step-ups, with onGround taken from the block cache rather than the packet flag. The Hypixel mode's +12 C04 presents a yDistance of 12 against a jump-scale allowance, so the envelope violation is immediate and the check set-backs the player; the onGround false flag does not help because the cache decides ground truth. This is the direct counter to the default mode, while the Motion mode's capped descent stays inside the envelope because it moves slower than gravity, which a maximum-style bound permits.

countering.label: Flight (ascension budget)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's Flight checks ascending moves against an ascend-distance budget measured from the ground location, an ascend-time count of ascendingMoves over maxAscendTime, and a per-move vertical speed cap, and its vertical-clip branch scans solid blocks between the safe and current locations whenever a vertical move exceeds 0.99 blocks. A 12-block C04 is far beyond the jump-scale vertical cap, so the Ascension branch fires on the first lift, and every repeated lift extends the ascending move count; in open void the clip branch stays quiet because no solids sit in the column, but the ascension ledger does not need it.

countering.label: MorePackets (movement packet rate)
countering.explanation: MorePackets scores raw movement packets into half-second buckets against an EPS max of 22 with 20 ideal, plus a burst path on the newest bucket. The catch stream adds roughly one C04 per 9 ticks, about 2.2 per second, on top of the vanilla 20 C03s, which sits right at the 22/s ceiling: the window accumulator stays marginal and only tighter server configs or a burst of repeated catches trip it. It is an honest boundary rather than a direct hit, included because the periodic lifts are the module's only packet-rate signature.

countering.label: moving NoFall (server fall-height ledger)
countering.explanation: NCP's moving NoFall tracks its own fall height from the move stream and, on landing, deals damage computed from that server-side height, resetting the ledger only when the height warrants no damage. The module's client-side fallDistance = 0 write is invisible to it: NCP never reads the client's fall distance, so the reset neither delays damage nor clears the ledger, and in the void where there is no landing the ledger simply grows. The entry frames the both-sides truth: the reset is local fiction, and the real protection is the C04 lift, which the envelope checks above already flag.
